data.title: S&P 500 Touches All-Time High After Jobs Report Surprise
data.description:
The S&P 500 opened in record territory on Friday, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded slightly lower after a weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs report reshaped expectations for Federal Reserve policy, according to Friday market data.

The benchmark S&P 500 gained about 0.5% to trade above its previous record closing high, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed roughly 1.1%. The Dow, meanwhile, slipped about 0.1% in morning trading as investors weighed signs of a cooling labor market against the prospect of lower interest rates.

Fresh employment figures showed the U.S. economy unexpectedly lost jobs in July, prompting Treasury yields to decline as traders reduced expectations for another near-term Federal Reserve rate increase. The softer data helped lift technology shares, while investors also looked ahead to upcoming inflation reports for further policy clues.

Despite the Dow's modest decline, broader market sentiment remained constructive, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq supported by falling bond yields and continued optimism surrounding large-cap technology stocks.

Wendy's Stock Rises Despite Dividend Cut and Outlook Withdrawal
data.description:
Wendy's , a global quick-service restaurant chain, pulled its full-year guidance and chopped its dividend in half, yet the stock still climbed about 1.7% in Friday trading. Investors appeared willing to give new management the benefit of the doubt, but the operating numbers were hard to ignore. U.S. systemwide sales sank 8.2%, domestic same-restaurant sales slid 7% and international systemwide sales rose just 3.4%. The message is clear: Wendy's biggest market is losing momentum, and overseas growth is nowhere near strong enough to fill the gap.

The pressure showed up across the income statement. Net income crashed 40.8% to $32.6 million, while adjusted EBITDA dropped 15.4% to $124.1 million. Company-operated restaurant margin narrowed 2.4 percentage points to 13.8% as softer customer traffic collided with higher food and labor costs. Management also cut the quarterly dividend from $0.14 to $0.07 per share, freeing up roughly $53 million a year based on about 190 million shares outstanding. New CEO Bob Wright is betting that cash is better spent fixing menus, marketing, digital capabilities and franchise economics than paying shareholders while the business is under pressure.

The GF Value chart makes the stock look ridiculously cheap at first glance. With shares trading around $7.46 versus a GF Value estimate of $18.44, Wendy's appears to be nearly 60% below fair value. That kind of discount usually grabs investors' attention. But there's a catch. GuruFocus also labels the stock as a possible value trap, a reminder that cheap stocks often get cheaper when the business keeps deteriorating. Pulling guidance, slashing the dividend and fighting falling traffic are not the ingredients of a clean turnaround. If management can rebuild sales and restore margins, today's price could prove attractive. If not, that "bargain" may simply be the market correctly pricing in more pain ahead.

SpaceX Jumps 10% as Lockup Fears Ease
data.description:
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX, Financials), Elon Musk's space and AI company, jumped more than 10% as investors grew more comfortable with the stock after its first major post-IPO lockup expiration.

Shares had already gained 6% Thursday even as the number of shares available for trading more than doubled. That matters because investors had worried the sudden increase in supply could trigger another sharp selloff. Instead, the stock held up and extended its rebound Friday.

SpaceX is still trading below its $135 IPO price after a volatile stretch that erased hundreds of billions of dollars in market value.

The risk is not gone. Another 7% of shares are scheduled to unlock on Aug. 21, and the tradable float is expected to keep rising through December.

Investors also remain focused on heavy AI spending and the company's lack of profitability. For now, though, the market appears to be treating the first unlock as less damaging than feared.

ELEKTROS Inc. (Ticker:ELEK) today reiterated its continued focus on advancing its hard-rock lithium mining initiatives, electric vehicle charging patent strategy and broader long-term strategic growth objectives.

The Company remains confident that this summer's dynamic market backdrop has sparked renewed enthusiasm across numerous areas of the public markets, including microcap and penny-stock companies positioned around next-generation industries. ELEKTROS remains confident that increasing recognition of its rare-earth and critical-minerals vision, its hard-rock lithium initiatives in Sierra Leone and its advanced EV charging intellectual property is helping present the Company to an increasingly broad community of retail, microcap and institutional investors worldwide.

Management remains confident that the global transition toward electric mobility, battery storage and next-generation charging infrastructure continues to create compelling long-term opportunities throughout the lithium and EV ecosystem. The Company further remains confident that attractive market entry points can encourage investors to study emerging companies at an early stage; however, ELEKTROS emphasizes that all investment decisions should be made only after careful, independent due diligence and consideration of each investor's individual financial circumstances and risk tolerance.

Recent reporting by the Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal and China Daily has underscored the increasing importance of lithium supply chains, battery materials, refining capacity and EV infrastructure as global demand continues to expand.

ELEKTROS continues to pursue hard-rock lithium opportunities in Sierra Leone while advancing United States Patent No. 12,522,100 B1, relating to advanced electric vehicle charging technology designed to improve charging efficiency and reduce charging times.

Elon Musk has previously stated: "It is definitely true that the fundamental enabling technology for electric cars is lithium-ion as a cell chemistry technology. In the absence of that, I don't think it's possible to make an electric car that is competitive with a gasoline car."

The Company also continues to assess strategic opportunities involving its patent portfolio, including potential licensing discussions and other strategic alternatives, while maintaining its commitment to protecting its intellectual property.

Lilly and Novo Win a Key GLP-1 Antitrust Fight
data.description:
Eli Lilly and Co. (LLY, Financials), the drugmaker behind Zepbound, won a legal victory alongside Novo Nordisk after a federal judge dismissed an antitrust lawsuit over access to compounded GLP-1 drugs.

Compounding pharmacy Strive Specialties had argued that Lilly and Novo used exclusive telehealth partnerships to make it harder for doctors to prescribe customized alternatives to their branded treatments.

Judge Micaela Alvarez rejected the claim, finding that Strive had not shown the kind of antitrust injury needed to proceed because compounded products do not compete in the same market as Zepbound and Wegovy.

For Lilly and Novo, the ruling removes one challenge to how they distribute some of the most valuable drugs in the pharmaceutical industry.

The fight is not necessarily over. Strive said it is considering an appeal. Investors will continue watching legal battles around compounded GLP-1 drugs as demand for weight-loss treatments keeps expanding.
